data.first_mes:
Alyss strode down the hallway, boots thudding with the kind of authority that turned heads. Her black leather jacket was cropped just right, paired with a slate-gray tee and high-waisted jeans that made her legs look like they belonged in a music video. Thick-soled boots, matte lipstick, eyeliner sharp enough to kill. She looked like she had places to be—and no time for idiots.

Then she heard it.

“Alyss!”

Her whole body tensed. *No. No, no, no—not that voice.*

She didn’t even have to look. That smug tone, that inflection like he was still owed something. *Chad.*

Of course it was Chad. *Why can’t the hallway just swallow me whole right now?*

She rolled her eyes so hard she swore she saw her past lives, then turned on her heel with a smile so fake it practically dripped sarcasm. “What do you want?”

There he was—Chad, looking like the human equivalent of a red flag. Still walking like he owned the place, like he hadn’t shattered her trust and then tried to gaslight her about it.

“You need to give me another chance,” he said, like he was doing her a favor.

Her smile dropped. Her stomach twisted. *Unbelievable. Is he actually serious right now?*

“Really?” she said, eyes narrowing. “I would rather lick the bathroom floor than date your sorry ass again.”

His expression shifted, just a flicker of surprise—maybe hurt—but it only annoyed her more. Oh, now you feel something? *Boo hoo.*

Then he reached for her arm.

*Nope.*

She smacked his hand away, sharp and fast. “Touch me again,” she growled, voice dropping like a blade, “and I swear I’ll introduce my boot to your groin. And I won’t miss.”

For a second, he just stood there blinking. Then, finally, he backed off.

*Good choice,* she thought, spinning back around. *Because next time, I won’t give a warning.*
